items.title: CW-Net gives humans interpretable explanations of self-driving car decisions
items.summary_en: MIT CSAIL and AeroAstro researchers, working with autonomous-vehicle company Motional, developed CW-Net, a 'concept-wrapper' classifier that translates a black-box AV motion planner's reasoning into human-interpretable concepts (e.g. 'approaching stopped vehicle', 'close to cyclist'). In closed-track tests and a larger simulation study, these explanations helped both safety drivers and non-expert users more accurately predict the vehicle's next move, which the researchers say could improve trust and safety around AV mistakes.
items.notes: Peer-reviewed paper published in Nature (2026); co-senior author Julie Shah directs CSAIL's Interactive Robotics Group. Content verified via MIT News search snippets and mirrored coverage on MIT AeroAstro and EurekAlert (press-release syndication); direct WebFetch of news.mit.edu was blocked by network egress rules in this session.

items.title: MIT CSAIL's xvr technique speeds up X-ray-to-3D-scan alignment for surgical navigation
items.summary_en: A CSAIL-led team headed by postdoc Vivek Gopalakrishnan developed xvr, a patient-specific AI method that rapidly aligns intraoperative X-rays with preoperative 3D scans for orthopedic and neurosurgical navigation. By pretraining a foundation model on synthetic X-rays generated from over 2,000 patient volumes, xvr cuts per-patient fine-tuning from hours to about five minutes, and the team reports it outperforms prior AI methods by roughly an order of magnitude across patients, body parts, and procedures.
items.notes: Peer-reviewed paper published in Nature (2026). MIT says it is collaborating with surgical robotics companies and clinical groups toward deployment. Content verified via MIT News search snippets and mirrored coverage on MIT Schwarzman College of Computing and EurekAlert; direct WebFetch of news.mit.edu was blocked in this session.

items.title: MIT affiliates detail ties to renamed MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab for AI and quantum tech transfer
items.summary_en: MIT News profiled how MIT researchers, including CSAIL senior research scientist Aude Oliva (who serves as MIT director of the lab), engage with the newly renamed MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab -- formerly the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab -- to bring academic AI theory into IBM's production systems. The rename reflects an expanded scope that now includes quantum computing alongside the lab's original AI research focus.
items.notes: Institutional feature on lab collaboration/tech-transfer rather than a single new research paper. Details drawn from MIT News search-result snippets only; the full article could not be fetched directly because news.mit.edu was blocked by this session's network egress proxy, so wording should be treated as an approximate paraphrase pending verification against the original.
